items.title: Cart quantity/remove button rules using :contains() (never valid CSS)
items.why: All three rules (+/- quantity links, quantity number, REMOVE link) use `:contains()` in every selector. `:contains()` exists only in jQuery, no browser supports it in CSS, and one invalid selector invalidates the whole rule, so Chrome drops all three rules (33 !important declarations). They have never applied.
items.proof: grep shows `:contains(` only on baseline lines 2439-2441, 2458-2460, 2474. The rules are top level (brace depth 0). Headless Chrome keeps 881 top-level rules with or without this block, byte-identical. A control test (removing the live checkout rule right after it) is detected (880).
items.verify: IDENTICAL: Chrome keeps exactly the same rules in the same order. No visual change is possible.
items.visual_change: None. Keep the `/* 5. Neumorphic Checkout Button` rule that follows: it is live.
items.notes: Ziko may already have deleted this manually in Shopify admin. If apply.py says the text is not found, check whether the block is already gone; if so mark DONE.

items.title: .site-header rule swallowed by a comment that lost its opening /*
items.why: The banner comment 'GLASSMORPHIC ADVANCED NAVIGATION SYSTEM' is missing its opening `/*`. Its text (`GLASSMORPHIC ... ==== */`) becomes part of the next selector, which is invalid, so Chrome drops the whole `.site-header { position: sticky; ... padding: 8px 18px; z-index: 50; }` rule.
items.proof: Verified by two agents and headless Chrome: the rule is absent from the parsed rule list; removing these lines leaves Chrome's rule list identical (see Verify).
items.verify: IDENTICAL: Chrome keeps exactly the same rules in the same order. No visual change is possible.
items.notes: Do NOT fix it by adding the missing `/*`. That would switch on a .site-header rule that has never been live and change the header.

items.title: First of two identical @keyframes marquee definitions
items.why: `@keyframes marquee` is defined twice at top level (baseline 978-981 and 3021-3028). When names repeat, only the last definition is used, so this one never runs. Both definitions are identical (translateX(0) to translateX(-50%)).
items.proof: Brace-depth scan: both at depth 0, before the unclosed @media. No @layer/@supports/@container in the file. Only consumer: `.announcement-bar .announcement-bar__track { animation: marquee 22s linear infinite !important }`.
items.verify: DIFFERENT /   - removed: @keyframes marquee {  /   0% { transform: translateX(0px); } /   100% { transform: translateX(-50%); } / }
items.visual_change: None. Keep the `/* === KEYFRAMES === */` comment and `@keyframes trustIconBounce` that follow.

items.title: `#MainContent > .shopify-section:first-child { background: #e5efea !important }` always loses
items.why: Its only declaration always loses to rules in the same file that match the same element: line 78 (same specificity, later, also !important) and line 310 (`#MainContent` x48 `>.shopify-section:first-child{background:#f2f2f2!important}`, far higher specificity). #e5efea never renders.
items.proof: Same file, so stylesheet load order does not matter. No media queries involved. Checked in headless Chrome by changing the value to a sentinel: computed background unchanged.

items.title: `.all-products-btn:hover` accidentally nested inside `.all-products-btn`
items.why: The `.all-products-btn {` rule is not closed before the hover rule, so the hover rule is nested. With CSS nesting it means `.all-products-btn .all-products-btn:hover` (a button inside a button), which the theme markup never has. The intended hover style (gradient border, scale 1.12) has never applied.
items.proof: Headless Chrome serializes it as `& .all-products-btn:hover` inside `.all-products-btn`. Theme markup uses .all-products-btn without nesting (index sections and templates/404.liquid).
items.verify: DIFFERENT /   - removed: .all-products-btn { /   color: rgb(12, 12, 12) !important; letter-spacing: normal !important; animation: auto ease 0s 1 normal none running none !important; padding: 1.016rem 2.71rem !important; font-size: 17.618px !important; background: linear-gradient(rgb(249, 250, 251), rgb(249, 250, 251)) padding /   - removed: CSSStyleRule(.all-products-btn) > & .all-products-btn:hover { color: rgb(12, 12, 12) !important; border: 1px solid transparent !important; background: linear-gradient(rgb(249, 250, 251), rgb(249, 250, 251)) padding-box padding-box, linear-gradient(135deg, rgb(255, 41, 148), rgb(33, 213, 237)) border /   + added:   .all-products-btn { color: rgb(12, 12, 12) !important; letter-spacing: normal !important; animation: auto ease 0s 1 normal none running none !important; padding: 1.016rem 2.71rem !important; font-size: 17.618px !important; background: linear-gradient(rgb(249, 250, 251), rgb(249, 250, 251)) padding-b
items.visual_change: None expected. HIGH confidence, not mathematically proven: it depends on markup (an app could in theory inject nested buttons).
items.notes: REVIEW: ask Ziko first. The edit replaces the nested block with a single `}` that closes the parent rule, so the parent's own declarations stay exactly the same.

do_not_apply.title: Unclosed @media in toylvia.css (real bug, but fixing it CHANGES the site)
do_not_apply.text: Baseline line ~5535 opens `@media (max-width: 1024px) {` with a dangling `.cat-ice-label` selector and never closes it. Everything after it (about 670 lines: outlined Add to Cart pill, transparent header, free shipping bar, cart bundle, badge colours, mobile crash fix, ...) only applies at widths <= 1024px. Fixing it would switch those styles ON for desktop. Ask Ziko whether he wants that before touching it.
